name: Virtual

hero.title: A hundred thousand rows. Twenty in the DOM.
hero.lede: TanStack Virtual with its state in Pyreon signals. Only the rows on screen exist, and a scroll adds the rows coming in and removes the ones going out: the rows that stay do no work, because there is no component to re-render.

items.title: Scrolling touches the edges only
items.text: Rows render through a keyed `<For by={(r) => r.index}>`. A scroll step creates the rows entering and removes the rows leaving; the rest keep their DOM and run nothing.

items.title: Signals out, signals in
items.text: `virtualItems()`, `totalSize()` and `isScrolling()` are signals, and the options are a function that reads signals. Filter the list and `count` re-sizes the virtualizer on its own.

items.title: Any row shape
items.text: Fixed heights, known variable heights, or measured on render with `measureElement`. Horizontal lists and masonry lanes too, from the same core TanStack uses.

items.title: Jump anywhere
items.text: `instance.scrollToIndex(50_000)` for "go to row", `scrollToOffset` for a saved position.

difference.title: Same core. No list re-render per scroll step.

before.label: React + @tanstack/react-virtual
before.caption: Each scroll step re-renders the list component and reconciles every visible row.

after.label: with @pyreon/virtual
after.caption: The component runs once. A scroll step adds and removes rows at the edges.

comingFrom.title: Options become a function; getters become signals.
comingFrom.before:
const v = useVirtualizer({
  count: rows.length,
  getScrollElement: () => parentRef.current,
  estimateSize: () => 40,
})

v.getTotalSize()
v.getVirtualItems()
v.scrollToIndex(5000)
comingFrom.after:
const v = useVirtualizer(() => ({
  count: rows().length,
  getScrollElement: () => scrollEl ?? null,
  estimateSize: () => 40,
}))

v.totalSize()
v.virtualItems()
v.instance.scrollToIndex(5000)
comingFrom.note: Every `@tanstack/virtual-core` option works the same (`overscan`, `horizontal`, `lanes`, `gap`, `paddingStart`, `measureElement`…). The `Virtualizer` instance is on `.instance`; its state is mirrored into the `virtualItems`, `totalSize` and `isScrolling` signals.

features.title: Virtualization, the TanStack way, with signals.

items.name: `useVirtualizer`
items.text: For a scrolling element; returns `virtualItems`, `totalSize`, `isScrolling` and the core `instance`.

items.name: `useWindowVirtualizer`
items.text: For a list that scrolls with the page; safe to render on the server.

items.name: Reactive options
items.text: Read a signal in `count` and the virtualizer follows. Changed a size estimate? One `instance.measure()` re-sizes the list.

items.name: `item(index)`
items.text: Per-index `start`, `size` and `lane` accessors for measured rows, at no cost until you use them.

items.name: Measured rows
items.text: `measureElement` corrects an estimate once a row renders.

items.name: Horizontal and lanes
items.text: `horizontal: true` for carousels, `lanes` for masonry grids.

items.name: `scrollToIndex` / `scrollToOffset`
items.text: Go to row 50,000, or back to where the user was.

items.name: Overscan
items.text: Render a few rows past each edge so fast scrolls do not flash blank.

items.name: Detached at mount
items.text: A scroll element inserted after mount (a `<Show>`, a portal) gets its observers re-attached instead of rendering zero rows.

recipes.title: A filtered contact list
recipes.text: The count reads a computed, so typing in the search box re-sizes the list and keeps only the visible matches in the DOM.

recipes.title: A feed that scrolls with the page
recipes.text: No inner scroll box: the window is the scroller, and rows of different heights are measured as they render.

api.title: Two hooks and the TanStack core.

limits.title: Give a close `estimateSize`
limits.text: The scrollbar is sized from it before rows are measured. A close guess keeps the thumb from jumping.

limits.title: Find-in-page sees rendered rows only
limits.text: Rows outside the window are not in the DOM, so the browser's search cannot find them. Put a search box on long lists.

limits.title: Key rows by index
limits.text: Use `<For by={(item) => item.index}>` so a scroll moves only the edges. A `.map()` without a `key` rebuilds every visible row.

limits.title: Native lists are already lazy
limits.text: On iOS and Android (native targets are experimental), put a `<For>` as the only child of `<Scroll>` and it becomes a `LazyVStack` or `LazyColumn`, no virtualizer needed. `@pyreon/virtual` itself is web.

faq.q: How does it compare with react-virtual?
faq.a: Same `virtual-core`, rendered differently. In real Chromium at 10,000 rows, one run: mount 1.15×, 60 scroll steps 1.04×, jump to row 5,000 1.10×, unmount 3.25× faster. Under happy-dom the record shows scroll-to-DOM 1.4× faster and mount 1.1× slower; happy-dom is a JavaScript DOM, the browser figure is the one that counts.

faq.q: Do I need it for a table?
faq.a: For a few hundred rows, no. Past a few thousand, pair it with `@pyreon/table`: virtualize the row model and render only the window.

faq.q: Does it work with server rendering?
faq.a: `useWindowVirtualizer` checks for a browser before touching `window`, and both hooks start measuring on mount, so the server renders the list shell and the client fills the window.
Yes. Pass a per-index `estimateSize`, or measure rows with `measureElement` and a `data-index` attribute, as in TanStack.

benchmarks.p: Same `virtual-core` on both sides, so the difference is rendering: React re-renders the list on every scroll step, Pyreon patches the rows entering and leaving.
